attacks.claim: A vendor redelivery that reuses the original signed timestamp and arrives more than 5 minutes later will be rejected with 401 every time. The artifact does not say whether PlugCloud re-signs retries, so backlog readings could be dropped. This is unverified vendor behaviour, not a demonstrated failure.
attacks.evidence: rejects deliveries more than 5 minutes old or in the future, and returns a bare 401 on any failure

attacks.claim: The claim that startup fails when the secret is missing or short is not shown. The route resolves settings through a per-request Depends(get_settings), so validation may only run on the first webhook request unless the app instantiates Settings at startup.
attacks.evidence: startup fails if it is missing or short; settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)

attacks.claim: The route test assumes the client fixture overrides get_settings so the server verifies with the fixture's secret. The conftest diff only changes the settings constructor. If the override is missing, the signed request in the route test gets 401 and the test fails.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no dependency_overrides for get_settings in the tests/conftest.py diff; test_route_rejects_unsigned_and_accepts_signed signs with settings.plugcloud_secret

attacks.claim: Rejections are logged at warning level with no counter or alert. A clock-skewed host or a rotated vendor secret would silently reject all readings. There is also no rotation path: the secret is a single value and changing it needs an env edit and restart.
attacks.evidence: log.warning("plugcloud webhook rejected: %s", exc); ABSENT: alerting, metrics, or key-rotation guidance

attacks.claim: Body parsing moved out of FastAPI's model binding, so the 422 response shape for malformed payloads changed from FastAPI's default to a custom detail string. Any client or test relying on the old shape will break. Nothing in the diff updates such tests.
attacks.evidence: raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="invalid payload") from None

attacks.claim: The body is read fully into memory before the signature check. The 1 MB proxy cap bounds this, but the app itself applies no limit, so the cap is the only defence against large unauthenticated bodies.
attacks.evidence: body = await request.body() (the 1 MB limit is at the reverse proxy, not in the diff)
